name: Raffles Makkah Palace
positioning: All-suite Raffles hotel in the Abraj Al Bait Complex overlooking the Holy Kaaba and Masjid Al Haram, with 24-hour Raffles Butler Service
best_for: Pilgrims on Hajj or Umrah who want a suite overlooking the Kaaba
Travelers who want a dedicated 24-hour butler
Families who want guided tours of Makkah's historical and religious sites

facts.text: Raffles Makkah Palace is an all-suite hotel overlooking the Holy Kaaba and Masjid Al Haram.
Suites are designed in a comfortable residential style with Arabesque accents.
All suites come with 24-hour Raffles Butler Service.
Raffles Butlers are the guests' primary point of contact and know the hotel's services and the local vicinity.
Al Majlis serves Mediterranean cuisine prepared simply, in the classic Italian way.
In-suite dining is available 24 hours a day.
Raffles Spa has female and male spa and gym facilities on the 11th and 12th floors.
The spa has sauna and steam rooms.
The hotel has a private prayer area.
The hotel offers prayer facilities overlooking Al Masjid Al Haram.
Return transfers to and from Jeddah's Abdulaziz International Airport can be arranged on request.
The hotel is close to Jabal Al Nour, the Mountain of Light, as well as Al Jamarat and Jabal Thawr.

highlights.text: Al Majlis has an outdoor terrace overlooking the Grand Mosque and the Kaaba.
The hotel is part of the Abraj Al Bait Complex, alongside a four-storey luxury shopping centre, a prayer hall, a convention centre, a museum and a lunar observatory.
Private elevators within the hotel are exclusively for Raffles Makkah Palace guests.
The hotel arranges custom tours to Makkah's historical areas and main religious attractions, including excursions and events for children.
The Majestic Suite has Kaaba views, two living rooms and its own prayer room.

considerations.text: The hotel is approximately a 5-minute walk from Al Masjid Al Haram; dedicated elevators in the Clock Towers Complex lead directly to the ground floor.
WhataHotel notes the hotel is in an extremely busy pilgrimage area during Hajj season.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the ultra-luxury positioning.
